identity.title: GnnXemplar: Exemplars to Explanations - Natural Language Rules for Global GNN Interpretability

problem.claim: The paper addresses global interpretability of GNN node-classification predictions through explanations that characterize an entire class.

gap.claim: The authors state that global explanation methods are underdeveloped, while motif-based explainers struggle with large real-world graphs, rare subgraph repetition, high-dimensional attributes, and complex structure-attribute interactions.

contributions.claim: GnnXemplar selects representative nodes in GNN embedding space and generates natural-language rules from their neighborhoods.
It formulates exemplar selection as coverage maximization over reverse k-nearest neighbors and provides an efficient greedy approximation.
It uses a self-refining LLM prompting strategy to derive interpretable rules.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present GnnXemplar as a novel global explainer inspired by Exemplar Theory from cognitive science.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments across diverse benchmarks show significantly higher fidelity, scalability, and human interpretability than existing methods.
The authors report that human interpretability was validated in a user study involving 60 participants.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN opacity limits trust and adoption in node classification.
Local explanations do not resolve the underdevelopment of class-level global explanations.
Motif discovery is described as poorly suited to large, attribute-rich graphs with complex structure-attribute interactions.
GnnXemplar combines embedding-space exemplars, reverse-k-nearest-neighbor coverage, greedy selection, and self-refining LLM prompts to produce natural-language rules.
The authors report improvements over existing methods and user-study validation with 60 participants.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a scalable selection objective with a separate natural-language rule-generation mechanism, and reports both system-level metrics and a 60-person interpretability study.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests a useful way to connect computational coverage, explanation construction, and human-facing evaluation in one argument.
lessons.application: For a global-interpretability paper, explicitly map the representative-selection objective to the explanation-generation step, then pair fidelity/scalability results with a targeted human-interpretability evaluation.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when explanations are intended solely for automated downstream use or when human judgments cannot be collected reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, metric definitions, effect sizes, baselines, or statistical details behind the reported improvements.
The user-study design, participant expertise, and validation procedure are not described.
The approximation guarantee or runtime details of the greedy method are unspecified.
